solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Terribly mundane around November, like some railway stations?

indicators.note: something done terribly is done badly, so the word that follows is knocked out of its proper order
around says the shuffled word wraps itself about the next piece, holding it inside

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged
N is November in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A grumble that some dull little railway stations are dreadfully boring places to pass through.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters give UNMANED, and N slots in after UNMAN to make UNMANNED.
explanation.definitionFit: Many small rural stations have no staff on duty, which is what being without crew or attendants describes.

clue.text: Happy state initially: no issues really, vehicle as new assuredly

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words that follow it

blocks.clueFragment: no issues really, vehicle as new assuredly
blocks.note: the first letters of these seven words, read in order

explanation.surface: A car buyer's bliss: a vehicle that is as good as new, with genuinely no problems.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism this is the ultimate condition of peace and release, and casually it means perfect bliss or contentment.

clue.text: Not silent, as broadcast permitted

indicators.note: something broadcast is heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: permitted means allowed, which is pronounced the same as the answer

explanation.surface: A note that something may be spoken on air because it has been approved.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking audibly, so others can hear, is the opposite of keeping quiet or saying words only in your head.

clue.text: Unhappy, oddly lacking sleep

indicators.note: lacking the odd-numbered positions means only the even-placed letters of the word survive

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters, once the first, third, fifth and seventh are dropped

explanation.surface: Someone miserable because, strangely, they have not been getting any rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A short doze taken during the day is a brief period of rest, a little slumber.

clue.text: Poor state, dire, is par sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the preceding letters are put into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written, as the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A golfer's lament that a dreadful round only managed par at best.
explanation.definitionFit: A building or object in poor condition through neglect, needing mending, is said to have fallen into this.

clue.text: Get rid of outdated alcoholic drink

blocks.note: first meaning: to dismiss someone from their job
second meaning: an old name for a dry white wine from Spain or the Canaries, as in Falstaff's favourite tipple

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one instruction to throw out an old bottle; really it is two separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a verb for firing an employee and an archaic noun for a fortified white wine similar to sherry.

clue.text: Provide funds for snoopers (not English) in new arrangement?

indicators.note: not English tells you to drop the letter that abbreviates English from the word beside it
a new arrangement means the remaining letters are put into a different order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the standard abbreviation for English, here removed

explanation.surface: A question of who might bankroll a band of spies, provided none of them are from England.
explanation.definitionFit: To back an event, team or person financially, often in return for publicity, is to underwrite or bankroll it.

clue.text: Family welcoming European with no record of offending

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so the first piece holds the second inside it

blocks.note: a clan is an extended family group
E is the standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A household takes in a foreign guest who has never been in trouble with the law.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a spotless criminal record, never convicted, is described informally as having this kind of sheet.

clue.text: Group finally visit port city

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word next to it

blocks.note: the final letter of visit
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian port, often shortened

explanation.surface: A party of travellers at last get to see a famous harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of three performers or people together forms a small ensemble or band.

clue.text: Very into disentanglement of Orpheus — it’s not difficult at all!

indicators.note: into says the first piece is put inside what follows
disentangling something pulls it apart and reorders it, so the name is rearranged

blocks.note: the mythical Greek musician, taken as written as letters to rearrange
V is the standard abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: Someone untangling the Orpheus myth, who finds the task surprisingly easy.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged name gives PUSHOER, and V goes in after PUSHO to make PUSHOVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A task that needs no effort, or an opponent easily beaten, is informally called an easy win or a walkover.

clue.text: Impressive set of cards and then some!

blocks.note: the cards dealt to one player in a game
taken as written

explanation.surface: A card player boasting of a great hand, and more besides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'And then some' is an idiom for 'and much more', which disguises the plain joining of two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Handsome can mean considerable or striking, as in a handsome win or handsome sum, so it matches impressive.

clue.text: Go beyond available resources, because of special purpose

blocks.note: as in a row over money, meaning because of it
SP is a common abbreviation for special
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A budget blown for a particular reason, like a one-off project.
explanation.definitionFit: To pay out more money than you have or than a budget allows is to exceed your means.

clue.text: Decline drink

blocks.note: first meaning: to go down, fall in level or health
second meaning: informal for downing a drink quickly, as in a pint

explanation.surface: Turning down the offer of a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decline' reads as refuse, but here it means to fall or sink lower.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to drop gradually lower and, colloquially, to swallow a beverage in one go.

clue.text: Remove front from prickly plant in leisurely stroll

indicators.note: taking away the front means the opening letter of the next word is dropped

blocks.note: a thorny shrub such as the blackberry

explanation.surface: Advice to clear a thorny bush out of the way on a gentle country walk.
explanation.definitionFit: A long relaxed walk in the countryside, with no hurry, is a hike or wander.

clue.text: Place of great activity, buzz?

blocks.note: surface reading: any busy, bustling spot such as an office or market
setter's reading: the buzz is literal, the hum of insects at home in their colony

explanation.walkthrough: 'Buzz' reads as excitement, but the question mark hints at the literal sound of bees.
explanation.definitionFit: The home of a bee colony is famously busy, so the word is also used figuratively for any bustling place.

clue.text: Like this clue, a trial?

blocks.note: taken as written
a cross to bear is a burden or trial

explanation.surface: A solver wondering whether this clue is going to be a real ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition refers to the clue itself: it is one of the horizontal entries in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: This clue is a horizontal entry in the grid, so it runs from left to right like its fellow entries.

clue.text: Matter recovered from lake — wild about that!

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first piece is wrapped around the other

blocks.note: savage means fierce or untamed
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Someone furious about what was dredged out of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods or material rescued from a wreck, fire or disaster are known by this name.

clue.text: Dad, zealous, carrying hand tool

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the letters sit inside the words before it

blocks.note: found running across the two words, ignoring the comma

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic father arriving with a tool in his hand.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an axe-like woodworking tool with its blade set at right angles to the handle, used for shaping timber.

clue.text: Make one’s home delightful at the outset? We will

indicators.note: at the outset points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: the opening letter of delightful
contracted form we'll, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A couple deciding that setting up house would be delightful, at least at first.
explanation.definitionFit: To live or reside somewhere is to settle and make a place your home, an older literary sense.

clue.text: Mob following extremely seismic game on board

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters
following means coming after, so the crowd is placed behind the letters taken from the next word

blocks.note: the outermost letters of seismic
a rabble is a disorderly crowd

explanation.surface: A crowd swarms in after an earthquake-sized shock aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' tells you the crowd comes after the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a word game played on a squared board, building interlocking words from lettered tiles.

clue.text: Moisten meat in bottom (about time!)

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first piece goes round the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: the base is the lowest part of something
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An impatient cook says it is high time the joint was moistened.
explanation.definitionFit: Spooning fat or juices over a roasting joint to keep it moist is the kitchen technique meant here.

clue.text: I’m received by temporary ruler’s group of soldiers

indicators.note: being received by someone means being taken in, so the first piece goes inside the next

blocks.note: a regent rules while the monarch is too young or absent
taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A soldier announces he has been granted an audience by the acting head of state.
explanation.definitionFit: An army unit, usually commanded by a colonel and made up of battalions, is a body of troops.

clue.text: Pull boat

blocks.note: first meaning: a sudden hard ... or heave
second meaning: a small powerful vessel that tows ships in harbour

explanation.walkthrough: The two words read as an instruction to haul a boat, but each defines the answer separately.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for yanking something hard and a noun for a harbour towing vessel.

clue.text: Photo that’s a match!

blocks.note: first meaning: an informal snapshot
second meaning: the call in a card game when two identical cards turn up, used generally for a pair

explanation.surface: Someone holds up a picture and declares it a perfect likeness.
explanation.walkthrough: Snap is a children's card game in which players shout the word when two matching cards appear.
explanation.definitionFit: It is casual for a quick photograph and also the cry used when two things are exactly alike.

clue.text: Reportedly moved fast in Tube?

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by others, so the words are taken by how they are heard

blocks.note: moved fast is flew, past tense of fly, which sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: A news report of someone racing along on the London Underground, known as the Tube.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tube' looks like the London Underground; here it is a plain pipe or duct.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimney duct carrying smoke and gases away from a fire or boiler is a kind of pipe.

clue.text: Poor writing in ledger, go bananas!

indicators.note: going bananas means going wild, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, doubling as part of the instruction's wording

explanation.surface: An accountant despairs at the scrawl in the account book and tells it to go crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go' does double duty: it is part of the fodder and of the phrase that signals the reordering.
explanation.definitionFit: This is comic or badly composed verse with clumsy rhythm and rhyme, so it counts as low-quality writing.
